To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD34 expression is lost in fibroblastic stroma surrounding breast carcinoma and that this loss is not a feature of fibroblasts surrounding benign lesions.
CD34 and SMA are not coexpressed in breast fibroblast and loss of CD34 expression is associated with invasive disease.
CD34 and SMA are not coordinately regulated in breast myofibrobalsts and that the loss of CD 34 is related to the malignant state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of breast cancer, and in particular with the role of stromal cells in the development and progression of the disease.
the role of the extracellular matrix in the pathogenesis of cancer and its role in the progression of cancer from a preinvasive to an invasive stage.
the role of the extracellular matrix in the development of invasive carcinoma and in particular the role of fibroblasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD34 expression is not specific for invasive carcinoma and is not a reliable marker of myofibrogenesis.
CD34 expression is not a reliable marker for myofibroplasia in breast lesions.
the loss of CD 34 in breast fibroblast is a feature of the malignant environment, and not of invasive disease per se.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
loss of CD34 expression is associated with invasive breast disease, but that the acquisition of SMA expression is a more frequent and generalised phenomenon.
the loss of CD 34 is not specific for the malignant environment and that radial scars may have a similar phenotype.
CD34 is a marker of normal and hyperplastic epithelial–stromal units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is more than one type of myofiboblast in the breast.
there is more than one type of myofiboblast in breast tissue, and this has implications for our understanding of the role of myofibrobasts in tumour development.
the acquisition of SMA expression by stromal fibroblasts is not limited to the peritumoral stroma but is seen in fibroadenomas and in radial scars.
